'''Ewan Clague''' (1896–1987) was the commissioner of the [[U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics]] (BLS) from 1946 to 1965.<ref name=bls>[http://www.bls.gov/bls/history/commissioners/clague.htm Commissioners: Ewan Clague] at bls.gov</ref><ref name=gm>Goldberg, Joseph P., and William T. Moye. 1985. ''[http://www.bls.gov/opub/blsfirsthundredyears/ First hundred years of the Bureau of Labor Statistics]''.  Bureau of Labor Statistics Bulletin 2235. U.S. Government Printing Office. {{ISBN|0-935043-01-2}}.</ref>

In 1952 he was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].<ref>[http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm View/Search Fellows of the ASA] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616161612/https://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm |date=2016-06-16 }}, accessed 2016-07-23.</ref>

==Early life and education==
Clague was born to [[Manx people|Manx]] immigrant parents and grew up on a homestead in Washington state.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1962/07/01/archives/personality-facts-not-politics-his-guide-clague-has-directed-labor.html|title=Personality: Facts, Not Politics, His Guide; Clague Has Directed Labor Statistics in 3 Administrations Shows Concern Over Misuse of Data His Agency Releases Even Looks Solid Praises His Staff Grew Up on a Farm|work=The New York Times|first=Joseph A|last=Loftus|date=1 July 1962|accessdate=10 October 2025}}</ref> Clague graduated from the [[University of Washington]] and earned a doctorate from the [[University of Wisconsin]].<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/1987/04/15/us/ewan-clague-90-us-labor-official.html Ewan Clague, 90; U.S. Labor Official], ''New York Times'', April 15, 1987</ref>
